canonicalJson.appliesTo: Every signed payload and every digest input (request bodies, envelopes embedded in other envelopes such as retry.revocation).
canonicalJson.notes: JCS is chosen over a bespoke canonicalizer specifically so unrelated, actively maintained JCS libraries exist for both .NET and JS/TS, removing whitespace/key-order/number-formatting disagreement as a source of cross-runtime signature mismatch.

requestSigning.description: Every mutating relay request signs a newline-joined base string over the request itself, independent of any envelope-level signature.
requestSigning.normalizedPath: Absolute path only (no scheme/host/query), percent-encoding normalized to uppercase hex digits, no trailing slash except '/'.
requestSigning.signatureAlgorithm: ECDSA-P256-SHA256, raw (r||s) format, 64 bytes, base64url-encoded without padding (86 characters).

nonce.scope: Unique per (deviceKeyId, nonce) pair; the relay rejects a reused nonce within the replay window regardless of timestamp.

socketAuth.description: collar/relay-messaging: the live connection to GET /v1/socket?device={deviceKeyId}. On accept the relay sends {type:"challenge", nonce, serverTime}; the client must answer with {type:"auth", deviceKeyId, signature} within authTimeoutSeconds, signing the base string with its device key (same signature format as requestSigning). The challenge is single-use, so no nonce row is written.
socketAuth.challengeNonce: 128 random bits, base64url without padding (22 characters)
socketAuth.keepAliveNote: WebSocket protocol keep-alive frames; the relay never wakes for them. The text message "ping" is answered "pong" without waking the relay either.

peerMessage.description: collar/relay-messaging: a frame between the two devices of a pairing. Static ECDH between the two device keys (as pairCharactersInfo) with its own HKDF info; the relay forwards it unread.
peerMessage.kdfInfo: "oathbound-relay-message-v1" || pairIdHash || pairEpoch (decimal), UTF-8 concatenation; salt is SHA-256(UTF-8 of pairIdHash + "|" + pairEpoch)
peerMessage.aad: JCS({pairIdHash, pairEpoch, from: "owner" | "sub", seq, sentAt}); these five travel in the clear in the frame
peerMessage.plaintext: Plain JSON {v: 1, kind: "command" | "notice", text, character: {n, w} | null, receipt?: true}; receipt is written only when true and only on owner commands, and a reader that doesn't know it ignores it
peerMessage.seq: Strictly increasing per pairing and direction; a sender uses max(last + 1, unix milliseconds) so a restored config can't reuse one

receipts.description: collar/command-receipts and the rulebook/oath decision notice. Both are ordinary sub -> owner notices (kind "notice") under every peerMessage rule; the relay can't tell them from other notices.
receipts.receiptText: collarreceipt <seq>:<a|r>[:<code>]( <seq>:<a|r>[:<code>])*; seq is the answered owner command frame's seq (decimal), a = applied, r = refused, and a refused entry carries exactly one code
receipts.asking: The sub answers only command frames whose plaintext has receipt: true, never notices or its own rulebook consequences
receipts.support: Each client lists "receipts" in features of its pairCharacters plaintext; an owner also treats a sub as supporting receipts after accepting one receipt from it
receipts.decisionText: collardecision rulebook accepted <version> | collardecision rulebook declined <version>[ <reason>] | collardecision oath accepted <oathId> | collardecision oath declined <oathId>; reason is whitespace-collapsed, at most 200 characters, and only on a declined version

peerChat.description: collar/relay-chat: a chat message between the two devices of a pairing (channel "chat" in a send). Same transport, routing and static ECDH secret as peerMessage, but its own HKDF info, its own seq space, no 2-minute age limit, and stored by the recipient's hub while it is offline. A frame without channel is "live" (a peerMessage).
peerChat.kdfInfo: "oathbound-relay-chat-v1" || pairIdHash || pairEpoch (decimal), UTF-8 concatenation; salt is SHA-256(UTF-8 of pairIdHash + "|" + pairEpoch)
peerChat.aad: JCS({channel: "chat", pairIdHash, pairEpoch, from, seq, sentAt})
peerChat.plaintext: Plain JSON {v: 1, kind: "chat", text} or {v: 1, kind: "image", text (caption, may be empty), image: {id, key, width, height}}
peerChat.seq: Strictly increasing per pairing and direction, separate from peerMessage seq; same max(last + 1, unix milliseconds) rule
peerChat.authFeature: The socket auth message carries features: ["chat"]; the relay stores or forwards chat only for a device that has declared it
peerChat.results: delivered | stored | mailbox_full | needs_update | over_limit | over_budget | refused; stored is followed later by a second ack for the same id with delivered or expired, kept for an offline sender until it reconnects

image.description: A picture in chat: the sender encrypts it with a fresh random key, uploads the ciphertext to POST /v1/chat-images/upload, and sends a kind "image" chat message carrying the id and key. The relay never holds the key.
image.idEncoding: 128 random bits, base64url without padding (22 characters), chosen by the sender
image.blob: nonce (12 bytes) || AES-256-GCM(ciphertext || tag) of the image file (JPEG or PNG) under a fresh 32-byte key; AAD = UTF-8 of "oathbound-chat-image-v1|" + id

mailboxStatus.description: Delivery receipts and sender statuses for every relay mailbox (catalog, rulebook, report), posted to POST /v1/mailbox/status as a mailbox-status envelope. A receipt (role "recipient") names the item it settles; a sender status (role "sender") says whether the sender can currently send. Codes are a fixed list and never carry content; they are visible to the relay, which needs role and sequence to release a held item.
mailboxStatus.signing: ECDSA-P256-SHA256 with the posting device's key over JCS of the envelope without signature (same rule as every signed envelope); the relay checks it and returns the envelope verbatim so the other member verifies it too.
mailboxStatus.capability: A sender applies receipt rules for a mailbox only once the pair status carries a recipient status for it signed by the pair epoch's receiver device; otherwise a consumed item counts as delivered.

legacy.description: Entries kept only for clients from before mailbox receipts (0.3.2.2 and older), which still use the catalog request/response flow. They are removed once the relay has logged no legacy_catalog_request for 14 days and at least 30 days have passed since the first plugin release that stopped creating catalog requests.
entries: vectors/crypto-vectors.json ecdhHkdfAesGcmCatalogEnvelope's catalog-response ciphertext case (its keys stay: the push and rulebook vectors reuse them)

capabilitySecrets.encoding: base64url without padding (43 characters) when transmitted; server stores only SHA-256(secretBytes) as capabilityId's paired hash.
capabilitySecrets.comparison: Constant-time hash comparison; the relay never logs or echoes the raw secret.
capabilitySecrets.invitationIdException: invitationId specifically uses 128 bits (base64url without padding, 22 characters) instead of the 256-bit default - it is single-use, short-lived (invitationExpirySeconds), and already bounded by the deviceInvitationCreate rate limit, so the smaller size still leaves guessing infeasible. Every other capability id (e.g. catalog requestId) keeps the 256-bit default.

proofDigest.description: The acceptance envelope's proofDigest is an opaque, single-use, exact-match token (compared for equality against the acknowledgement tell's carried value, never used as a content-integrity hash) - not a SHA-256 digest despite the name.

pairEpoch.type: non-negative integer, starts at 0 for a pair's first activation
pairEpoch.rule: Incremented every time a pairIdHash is re-activated after a prior revocation. Revocations, catalog requests/responses, and retries are valid only for the pair epoch they were issued under; anything from an older epoch is rejected.

monotonicSequence.revocationSequence: Strictly increasing per pairIdHash across all epochs; the relay and both clients reject a revocation whose sequence is not greater than the highest one already accepted for that pair.
monotonicSequence.snapshotId: Strictly increasing per pairIdHash within a pair epoch; the Owner rejects a catalog-response whose snapshotId is not greater than the last snapshot it successfully imported for that pair epoch.

keyAgreement.note: The Owner's ephemeral ECDH key travels in catalog-request; the Sub's ephemeral ECDH key travels in catalog-response. Neither is reused across requests.
keyAgreement.pushNote: catalog-push: the Owner publishes a signed catalog-mailbox-key receive key (rotated on every consume, so each decrypts at most one delivered snapshot); the Sub pairs it with a fresh ephemeral key per upload.
keyAgreement.rulebookNote: rulebook-push / rulebook-report: same scheme as catalog-push in each direction. The recipient (Sub for channel "rulebook", Owner for channel "report") publishes a signed rulebook-key, rotated on every consume; the sender pairs it with a fresh ephemeral key per upload.

kdf.pushInfo: "oathbound-relay-catalog-push-v1" || pairIdHash || receiveKeyId, UTF-8 concatenation (catalog-push only; catalog-response keeps the info above)
kdf.pairCharactersInfo: "oathbound-relay-characters-v1" || pairIdHash || pairEpoch (decimal), UTF-8 concatenation; salt is SHA-256(UTF-8 of pairIdHash + "|" + pairEpoch); the shared secret is static ECDH between the two members' device keys, so both derive the same key
kdf.rulebookInfo: "oathbound-relay-rulebook-push-v1" (rulebook-push) or "oathbound-relay-rulebook-report-v1" (rulebook-report) || pairIdHash || receiveKeyId, UTF-8 concatenation; salt is SHA-256(receivePublicKeyRaw || senderEphemeralPublicKeyRaw)

aead.nonceGeneration: CSPRNG per encryption, never reused for the same derived key
aead.pairCharactersAad: JCS({pairIdHash, pairEpoch, side: "owner" | "sub", seq}) of the record's request; the record is the plain JSON (no compression), stored as {nonce, ciphertext} base64url
aead.additionalAuthenticatedData: JCS(catalog-response envelope with ciphertextDigest/nonce/signature fields removed), binding ciphertext to its envelope metadata

compression.order: compress plaintext, then encrypt the compressed bytes; ciphertextDigest is SHA-256 of the final ciphertext (compressed+encrypted+tag)

pairingCode.description: collar/pairing code invitations. The code is shown and typed as Crockford base32 in groups of four; it is normalized (uppercase, dashes/spaces removed, I/L -> 1, O -> 0) and its UTF-8 bytes are the HKDF input keying material. The relay only ever sees SHA-256(lookupId).
pairingCode.lookupIdEncoding: base64url without padding (43 characters) of the HKDF output; used as the invitationId capability of a code invitation.
pairingCode.characterBlob: AES-256-GCM, 12-byte random nonce, plaintext = JCS of {name, world, triggerPhrase?, transport?}; transport is "relay-live-v1" from versions with live messaging, which refuse to pair with a side that omits it, AAD = UTF-8 of "oathbound-pair-code-v1|" + invitationId + "|" + ("inviter" | "accepter").

recoveryCode.description: collar/pairing-recovery. Same normalization and HKDF parameters as pairingCode; the relay only ever sees SHA-256(backupId).
recoveryCode.backupBlob: AES-256-GCM, 12-byte random nonce, plaintext = the client's backup JSON, AAD = UTF-8 of "oathbound-backup-v1|" + backupId.
